components.note: Original row note "currently left to an exercise" is superseded by a written composed proof: the clausal-form theorem is stated (SUP 116-125) and proved in the annex (ANX 108-175) by composing the on-route prenex theorem (full proof R 268-282), the Skolem equisatisfiability theorem (full proof R 331-430), the matrix clause construction (SUP 81-101) with its pointwise lemma (SUP 103-114, proof ANX 72-104), and the clause-closure equivalence proved in-line (ANX 142-163). All three listed goals are supplied (see GOAL-01..03).

Declared input is a first-order L-sentence (SUP 117) under nonempty-domain semantics (SUP 4-5, ANX 119, 147); the full pipeline NNF -> rectified NNF -> prenex NNF -> universal Skolem sentence -> CNF matrix -> clause set is stated (table rows 1-5 and 7; figure) and the open-formula closure caveat is stated (SUP 237-239, ANX 174).

evidence.label: lem:rectified-variant proof (fresh binder z outside V)

components.note: Freshness: rectification picks binders outside a finite forbidden set (SUP 144-145; R 125-126); the Skolem step introduces one fresh function symbol per existential position, arity = number of preceding universals, constants for initial existentials, giving a finite expansion L* (SUP 152-157; ANX 121-129; R 290-301); NNF/rectification/prenex/CNF/clause steps introduce no nonlogical symbols (SUP 141-151, 158-161, 166-169; ANX 116-117, 139-140, 77-78).

evidence.label: annex composition: AC expansion forward, choice-free reduct reverse
annex composition: both directions, no same-signature equivalence claim
definition Signature extension, expansion, and reduct

components.note: Directions stated: model of sigma -> expansion under AC; S-model -> L-reduct without choice; equivalence only for same-signature steps (NNF, rectification, prenex, matrix CNF/clause closure); the Skolem step is explicitly equisatisfiability, not formula equivalence.
